name: Djimini Senoufo
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog djim1235 names only Mensah & Tchagbale 1983 (Gur atlas, subclassification); no grammar/phonology of Djimini Senoufo (a tone language) with a stress statement located online.

sources.citation: M'Lanhoro, Joseph. 1985. Phonologie et morphologie verbale du djimini. Thèse de doctorat de 3e cycle, Université de Paris VII (dir. M. Houis & A. Culioli). 197 p. [CAMES deposit no. 00964; Glottolog ref 93450]
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing on word stress. Phonology part (pp. 9-84) = vowel inventory, consonant inventory, 'Inventaire des tons' (p. 59: four level tones H, MH, MB, B), tones of mono- and disyllables, tonal realisations on verbal bases and predicatives. No accent/stress section in the Sommaire (pp. 194-197); the only use of 'accent' is p. 80, 'l'accent tonal.. creuser l'écart entre deux tons.. un accent chantant', i.e. tonal-contrast enhancement, not stress placement. Full-text scanned a full-text search for stress/accent/intensité/proéminence/tonique found nothing else.
